title: BECE Business Studies: Office Practice - Business Studies - Departments in an Office
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The practice of breaking down a large organization into smaller units or sections based on specialized functions is known as
questions.explain: To ensure efficiency, large businesses use **departmentalization**, which is dividing the organization into specialized units or departments like Sales, Accounting, and Personnel.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The department that serves as the central hub of the organization, coordinating routine clerical work, managing general correspondence, and filing records is the
questions.explain: The **Administrative department** oversees general office management, receives and routes correspondence, manages records, and ensures the office runs smoothly on a daily basis.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The primary function of the Purchasing department is to
options: recruit new workers for the factory
buy raw materials and equipment at the best prices
prepare the company's annual financial budget
questions.explain: The **Purchasing department** is strictly responsible for sourcing, negotiating, and buying the right quality and quantity of raw materials and office equipment at the best possible price.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which department is responsible for keeping books of accounts, processing payrolls, and settling business invoices?
questions.explain: All financial transactions, such as calculating staff salaries (payroll), paying invoices, and maintaining ledgers, are the core duties of the **Accounting department**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The department that ensures finished goods reach the final consumers and generates revenue for the organization is the
questions.explain: The **Sales department** (often combined with Marketing) is responsible for distributing and selling the company's products to customers to generate income.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Hiring, training, staff welfare, promotion, and discipline of employees are the statutory functions of the
questions.explain: The **Personnel department** (Human Resources) focuses on managing the workforce, which involves recruitment, training, welfare, and disciplinary actions.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: If a business organization decides to introduce a new product and wants to project its long-term future goals and expansion strategies, it will rely heavily on the
questions.explain: The **Planning department** handles the research, forecasting, goal-setting, and strategic long-term projects necessary for organizational growth.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which department ensures the proper coordination, maintenance, and fuelling of company vehicles for distributing goods and moving staff?
questions.explain: The management of vehicle fleets, drivers, fuel logistics, and vehicle repairs falls under the purview of the **Transport department**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All the following are core functions of the Personnel department EXCEPT
questions.explain: While the Personnel department handles recruitment, leave, and dispute resolution, **balancing the company's financial ledgers** is exclusively the duty of the Accounting department.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which department would most likely initiate the process of issuing a Local Purchase Order (LPO) to an external vendor?
questions.explain: A Local Purchase Order (LPO) is an official document requesting goods from a vendor. Because it deals with buying, it is initiated by the **Purchasing department**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A worker who wants to apply for a loan against their upcoming salary would typically need approval routed through the Personnel department to which other department?
questions.explain: Since loans and salary advances deal with cash payouts and adjusting payroll records, the request must eventually be processed by the **Accounting department**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The primary economic principle behind organizing a large office into different departments such as Sales, Accounting, and Purchasing is
questions.explain: Assigning specific tasks to different departments ensures that workers specialize in what they do best. This applies the economic principle of **division of labour and specialization**, maximizing efficiency.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: If a company produces high-quality products but consistently fails to make a profit because customers are unaware of the products, which department needs to improve its performance?
questions.explain: The responsibility for creating market awareness, advertising, and pushing products to consumers rests with the **Sales department** (or Sales and Marketing department).
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The department that closely monitors market trends, researches new competitors, and advises management on future threats to the business is the
questions.explain: Analyzing business environments to chart future goals and mitigate risks is a strategic function belonging to the **Planning department**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The Accounting department relies on source documents to post entries. From which department would it likely receive documents concerning the hiring of a new employee and their starting salary?
questions.explain: Because the **Personnel department** manages recruitment, they determine starting salaries and communicate these figures to the Accounting department for payroll preparation.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: To prevent a halt in production, which department must work hand-in-hand with the storekeeper to replenish stock immediately it drops to a minimum level?
questions.explain: The storekeeper tracks the stock levels, but the actual acquisition of new materials to restock the warehouse is the sole duty of the **Purchasing department**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following describes a typical interaction between the Sales and Accounting departments?
options: Sales determines the tax rates while Accounting sells the goods.
Accounting advertises the products while Sales prepares the balance sheet.
Sales generates revenue invoices from customers which Accounting records and banks.
Sales repairs the delivery vans while Accounting recruits the drivers.
questions.explain: The Sales department makes the transaction (generating invoices and collecting cash), and passes these records and funds to the Accounting department to be **recorded and banked**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All of the following are recognized departments in a standard large organization EXCEPT
questions.explain: Personnel, Transport, and Administrative are standard functional departments. **Imprest** is an accounting system for petty cash, not a standalone department.
questions.subject: Business Studies
